newsitem.title: INDIA: India government possible by April 20-United Front.
newsitem.headline: India government possible by April 20-United Front.

text.p: A senior official of India's United Front coalition said on Wednesday that there was a "distinct possibility" that a new government would be formed before April 20.

The official, who asked not to be identified, was asked by reporters to comment on the 1997/97 (April-March) budget, set to be taken up by parliament on April 21. "If a government can be formed, which is a distinct possibility, before the 20th, that budget will be handled by the new government," he said.

Congress, which triggered the fall of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's government last week, said on Monday that it would support a new United Front government provided the alliance named a new leader.
"There is no question of a coalition with the Congress party at all. The consensus is that there should be no coalition," the senior United Front official said.
The United Front's decision-making Steering Committee was set to meet on Thursday at 3 p.m. (0930 GMT) to discuss a possible leadership change.
"The consensus on change of leadership as demanded by Congress has not yet emerged. The Left parties are yet to take a view. They are meeting right now," he said.
